title: OpenBSD 8.0 arrives with security record still intact
gist: OpenBSD 8.0, the project's 61st release, adds Intel Arc A-Series support, a 512GB kernel address space on AMD64 and RISC-V vector support, while retaining a record of only two remote holes in the default install in over thirty years.

insights.claim: OpenBSD 8.0 adds Intel Arc A-Series graphics support and raises the AMD64 kernel virtual address space from 4GB to 512GB, enabling VRAM mapping above 4GB.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Modern GPU support broadens usability on a security-focused OS, though the audience remains niche.

insights.claim: The release adds ARM64 hibernation, RISC-V 'V' vector extension and Advanced Interrupt Architecture support, a new RPKI-to-router daemon rtrd(8), and up to 64 virtual CPUs per guest.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: RISC-V and RPKI router tooling indicate OpenBSD continues to serve network infrastructure and emerging-architecture use cases.

insights.claim: OpenBSD retired Loongson support because the port stopped working with the Clang 22 compiler, showing how toolchain changes force out low-maintenance architectures.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Small ports without maintainers are dropped when compilers move on, which is a risk factor for niche hardware ecosystems.

insights.claim: Theo de Raadt says OpenBSD has a record of more than thirty years with only two remote holes in the default install, a claim central to its brand.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: The narrow 'default install' definition is what makes the record defensible and it is the reason OpenBSD code such as OpenSSH and LibreSSL is widely reused.
insights.quote: “proud of OpenBSD’s record of more than thirty years with only two remote holes in the default install.”

insights.claim: The release ships LibreSSL 4.4.0 and OpenSSH 10.6, and follows a semiannual schedule dating to 1996.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Predictable cadence plus upstream-critical components make the project outsized relative to its install base.
